audit.why: Difficulty 7/10 fits a 50.34% win rate over 872 games: Brand owns levels 1-5 with W/E poke and the E-Q stun package, Ahri takes over once Spirit Rush and item burst arrive.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer level chart disagreed with the content layer and the packet at rows 4, 5 and 6: phases[4].side said Ahri while win[4] and packet said Brand, and phases[5]/[6] said Skill while win[5]/win[6] and packet said Ahri.
audit.why: Level 6 gives Brand Pyroclasm (100s) and the phases[4].why text already argues Brand wins that row; the item-phase rows belong to Ahri, whose first-item Charm-into-combo burst outpaces Brand's ramp. The content layer and the packet already agree, so only the full layer needed moving.
audit.corrected: phases[4].side -> Brand, phases[5].side -> Ahri, phases[6].side -> Ahri, with the two late whys rewritten to match the new verdicts. No paired win[N] edits are proposed because win[4]='Brand', win[5]='Ahri' and win[6]='Ahri' are already correct on disk.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and the decisive interactions were never stated: Charm's flat 12s cooldown, Sear only stunning ablaze targets, Pillar's 25% bonus on ablaze units, and Orb of Deception's true-damage return pass.
audit.why: Charm (E) is 12s at every rank, so its downtime is a fixed window Brand can count. Sear (Q) stuns only if the target is already ablaze, which makes E-first mandatory. Pillar of Flame (W) adds 25% damage to ablaze units, so the stunned body eats the full pillar. Ahri's Q deals true damage on the return, so stacking MR is the wrong answer. Essence Theft heals her every 9 minions, so Grievous Wounds timing decides long trades.
audit.corrected: Cooldown and interaction facts folded into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[0].d, dontsFull[2].d and breakdown.mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: 18 lint findings: 15 misgendered fields calling Ahri he/his/him, two copy-paste bleeds (dosFull[1].d = tradeGood, dontsFull[2].d = tradeBad), and the digit-free cooldowns field.
audit.why: champ-gender.js lists ahri as female; the bleed bullets promised one thing in the title and repeated an unrelated body.
No patch-specific claim is made in the text, so nothing to correct for 26.15.
